verdictText: **APPROVE-WITH-NOTES.** No blockers, no majors. Every registered behaviour is implemented, red-first proof is genuine, the census fits, the eight leaves and the unit's own lifecycle fields are the only changes, and 11 of 12 behaviour mutants are caught by the registered tests. Four minors (M1-M4) and notes N1-N5; none requires a change to this head. Per-class findings are in section 5; the carry-forwards for P2CG1C are in section 7.

reviewClassEvidence.note: The unit's five sensitive review classes, each with the reviewer's section 5 finding verbatim. All five pass; concurrency passes with carry-forward CF-C5.

authority.finding: **Authority.** Controls are accepted only on server-side operations (`applyHostIntentWithControls`, `appendControlledCommandBatch`, `appendWithExtension`'s third argument). The guest wire door `handleIntentLocked` and the socket binder are unchanged; no wire schema, Protocol type or `server.js` composition changed. The guard runs on the writer's own handle inside the writer-owned IMMEDIATE transaction after the recorded-id check and before `append()`, so a D-side `CampaignLaunchView.revalidate(db, preparation)`-style recheck would be genuinely pre-write under the file write lock, not a preflight. A store that cannot run a guard is refused typed before any event (both the plain batch store and the per-event fallback). An uncontrolled door can never observe `refused`; if it did, `throwCommitFailure` throws (fail closed, never a false success). PASS.

privacy.finding: **Privacy.** `toJournalBatch` and the command identity do not see the controls: the guarded and unguarded fixtures produce byte-identical `payload_json`/`event_digest` rows and identical `command_digest`, equal to `canonicalizeCommandIdentityV1(...)`; payload rows contain no `guard|onCommitted|afterRelease`. `ICampaignCommittedBatch` is a frozen plain identity (ids, digest, positions, count), carries no payload, is never a wire message and never reveals anything a client cannot already derive from its own command. `committed-unsettled.events` are the same sequenced server events the `committed` arm already returned; `commit-uncertain.error` and the `errors` list stay on the server side (resultOfDoor rethrows them on uncontrolled doors exactly as the baseline threw). `envelopeOf` narrowing and the private envelope path are untouched. PASS.

replay.finding: **Replay.** Journal bytes are independent of controls, so replay/rebuild from the journal is unaffected; the divergence path still rebuilds from the durable log and keeps the committed batch; the recovered receipt survives file reopen in both leaves; the drift fixture (`armRemovalApplyDrift`) is additive behind a flag that no pre-existing case sets and the five pre-existing pipeline cases pass unchanged. An uncertain commit is resolved only by readback (`getCommandReceipt` finds the committed removal in the injected post-COMMIT-throw case and finds nothing in the rollback case). PASS.

idempotency.finding: **Idempotency.** Branch-before-duplicate and prior-receipt order is preserved on both store operations; an exact retry answers from the original receipt with one journal effect, no second application, broadcast, guard run or notification, and the next door still runs (host and store tests). The in-transaction `recorded` check additionally protects the pre-check/transaction window (my probe). The sequence-fallback `commandId` (`campaign-cmd:<campaign>:<base>`) still never dedupes by design, unchanged; a `commit-uncertain` on such a command carries that generated id, which the journal does record, so readback remains possible. PASS.

concurrency.finding: **Concurrency.** `runExclusive`/`lockDepth` single-writer discipline is intact: `commitEvents` still throws without the lock; `applyHostIntentWithControls` takes the same lock; the guard and `afterCommit` run inside the IMMEDIATE transaction; `onCommitted` runs after the native COMMIT and before mapping, verification and publication (`owner-in-transaction:false`, independent-connection visibility); `afterRelease` runs after the lock chain has moved on (lockDepth 0). Ordering of duplicate/auth/validation is unchanged in both doors. The `AggregateError` and publish-to-all changes do not mask errors: a single failure still throws/returns the same error object, several are all retained in order, and every subscriber still receives every event. One sharp edge for successors: `afterRelease` is scheduled by promise continuation, so the next queued door may begin (up to its first await) before `afterRelease` runs; nothing in B depends on that, but D's reservation release must not assume ordering against the next door's guard (CF-C5). PASS with that carry-forward.

judgments: **commit-uncertain leaves the live projection untouched; readback is the owner's.** Correct. The projection was never moved before the append (scratch `expected` only), so leaving it is the baseline behaviour; a speculative re-read inside the door would have changed the existing `campaignHostSerialization` poisoned-store case, as the author found. The arm carries `commandId` and the original error, which is exactly what readback needs; `getCommandReceipt` resolves both directions in the tests. Note that the classification is deliberately conservative: a *known* pre-write throw (guard throw, thenable guard, stale branch, saved-record rewrite throw) is also reported as `commit-uncertain`, so the only "nothing was written" signal with certainty is the typed `refused` arm. That is fail-safe (readback finds nothing and the command may be retried under the same identity), but D's guard should return refusals rather than throw if it wants the precise arm (CF-C2). Accept.

**Cleanup failure classification.** Accept. `committed` + cleanup failure -> `committed-unsettled` with the intent's identity (null only when none exists) is the honest reading: the batch is durable, something after it failed. Two sharp edges, neither blocking: (a) a `lost-race`, `refused` or `commit-uncertain` outcome plus a cleanup failure is converted into a thrown `AggregateError` whose `errors` holds only the cleanup error and whose `cause` holds the outcome, so the primary uncertain error lives one level down and an answerable lost race becomes a throw; (b) D must read `cause` to recover the outcome. Record as M3 (documentary) and CF-C4.

**Behaviour changes (AggregateError; publish to all; divergence error kept alongside rebuild error; openLocked no longer ignores the outcome).** Accept. The single-failure case throws the identical object, so no existing `instanceof` consumer changes (grep finds no non-test `instanceof CampaignProjectionDivergenceError` or `instanceof AggregateError` anyway); the 340 related suites and 35 predecessor suites pass; delivering to every subscriber before rethrowing is strictly more faithful to "every committed event reaches every subscriber" and the error is still raised. `openLocked`'s new throw on the failure arms is equivalent to the baseline, where the same errors propagated out of `commitCampaignEventBatch` before the outcome was ever built.

**max-lines warning on JournalCampaignEventStore.ts (446).** Accept, same ruling as A2's 476: the rule is `warn`, `npm run lint` passes, and removing it would need a new module outside the eight-leaf restriction. The writer's existing warning moving 435 -> 445 is the expected cost of the shared body plus the two new operations. Record the measured numbers in the review receipt (M1).

**Refusal on uncontrolled doors throws.** Correct and fail closed. By construction no uncontrolled path produces `refused` (`commitEvents` without controls never returns it; the uncontrolled adapter wrapper throws, which surfaces as `commit-uncertain` and is rethrown). Keeping the throw rather than a silent mapping is the right choice.

**No rebase over #2212.** Accept. The admitted baseline is 3826f7cb; `merge-tree` against the current `origin/main` is conflict-free; none of the 14 files changed on main since the baseline (fog-history projection, tactical rail, AI occupancy, victory page) touches a leaf, a campaign sync/journal module, `units.json` or the proof selectors. The exact-main proof must still run on the actual merge commit, as always.

The guarded merge should require all 32 names `success` on the merge ref's head.

carryForwards.wording: **CF-C1 (borrowed seam contract).** `SQLiteEventJournalWriter.appendInBorrowedTransaction(raw)` is synchronous, requires `db.inTransaction === true` on the writer's own handle, shares `validatedIdentity` with the owning wrappers, and never begins, commits, releases a savepoint or notifies. C's ordered "campaign C IMMEDIATE then match M IMMEDIATE" must open the C transaction itself on the journal's handle and call this operation inside it; only that outer owner may announce the C commit, after its own COMMIT returns. Do not use `appendWithExtension`/`appendPreparedWithExtension` for the borrowed role: both own an IMMEDIATE transaction and, when nested, silently become a SAVEPOINT (unchanged baseline behaviour when no `onCommitted` is requested; refused before writing when one is).

**CF-C2 (refusal versus throw).** The only "nothing written with certainty" signal is the typed `refused` arm; any throw from the append (including a throwing guard, a thenable guard result, a stale branch or a saved-record rewrite failure) is classified `commit-uncertain {commandId, error}` and must be resolved by `getCommandReceipt` readback, never by compensation or a fresh command. A guard that wants the precise arm must return `{kind:'refused', reason}` rather than throw.

**CF-C3 (capability fail-closed).** Controls are honoured only by `JournalCampaignEventStore` over a `SQLiteEventJournalWriter`; `InMemoryCampaignEventStore`, a non-SQLite journal, and any store exposing `appendCommandBatch` without `appendControlledCommandBatch` are refused with `append-controls-unsupported` before any write, at both the adapter and the host (`commitEvents`, including the per-event fallback). C and D must not add a second capability flag or a boolean switch; the presence of `appendControlledCommandBatch` is the capability.

**CF-C4 (outcome consumption).** `applyHostIntentWithControls` answers `CampaignDoorOutcome = answered | committed | lost-race | refused | commit-uncertain | committed-unsettled`, and throws only for a door-level throw or a cleanup failure on a non-committed outcome, in which case the thrown `AggregateError.cause` is the outcome and `errors[0]` is the cleanup error (an identity conflict is mapped to `answered` inside the door). Consumers must switch exhaustively (typecheck enforces it through `throwCommitFailure`), must treat `committed-unsettled` as durable-plus-unfinished (errors retained in order: notification, divergence, rebuild, publishes, cleanup), and must never map any failure arm to a public success or a zero-append answer.

**CF-C5 (cleanup ordering).** `afterRelease` runs once per door after the single-writer lock chain has advanced (lockDepth 0) and after `onCommitted` and publication, but it is a promise continuation: the next queued door may already have started (up to its first await) when it runs. A reservation release placed in `afterRelease` must therefore be idempotent and observable by readback, and the next door's guard must tolerate a not-yet-released prior reservation by refusing (fail closed) rather than assuming order.

**CF-C6 (writer-level onCommitted).** At the writer, `appendWithExtension`'s `onCommitted` is called un-wrapped after COMMIT; a throw there rejects the promise although the batch is durable. The adapter wraps it into `notificationError`; any new direct writer caller must either not throw from `onCommitted` or wrap it the same way, and must not read a rejection as "nothing committed".

**CF-C7 (trust boundary).** Controls (`guard`, `onCommitted`, `afterRelease`) are server-only operation arguments; `toJournalBatch`, `canonicalizeCommandIdentityV1`, the private envelope and every Protocol/wire type are unchanged and must stay so. The identity-equality fixture (guarded versus plain journal rows and digests) in `JournalCampaignEventStore.test.ts` is the regression the successors should keep green rather than re-derive.

notes.wording: **N1:** without an `onCommitted`, `appendWithExtension` nested inside a caller transaction still degrades to a savepoint exactly as on the baseline; this preserves the existing 2-argument callers and is why the refusal is conditional. A guard-only controlled append nested that way would run its guard inside the savepoint and report `committed` without durability; no production caller can reach that today (JS is single-threaded and better-sqlite3 is synchronous, so a door never runs with the journal handle mid-transaction), and the `onCommitted` request D will supply forces the refusal.

**N2:** mutant M5 survived at the registered suites only because the store's out-of-transaction receipt pre-check shadows the in-transaction `recorded` check; my probe confirms the head's code is correct inside the window (guard 0, notify 0, one batch). Coverage gap, not a defect.

**N3:** the mock in `CampaignMatchHost.pipeline.test.ts` gains the `armRemovalApplyDrift` branch; it is the only edit to an existing line in either test leaf and no pre-existing case sets it; the five pre-existing pipeline cases pass at both red and green.

**N4:** `commit-uncertain` for the sequence-fallback identity carries the generated `campaign-cmd:<campaign>:<base>` id, which the journal records, so readback works; `committed-unsettled.commandId` from `applyHostIntentWithControls` uses the intent identity and is null only when the intent offers none.
**N5:** `validate-roadmap --next` prints U25 at this head; advisory only, the validator does not model the one-lane rule. Not a finding.
